pure-announcement.rationale: A project homepage blurb describing what OpenSLO is, not a launch, release note or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: slo-burn-rate-alerting covers alerting on SLOs, not a declarative YAML language for defining them, so this adds a thin but new fact.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Its single claim — OpenSLO is an Apache-2.0 YAML spec for declaring SLOs — is directly verifiable at the project site.

durability.rationale: The existence of a vendor-neutral SLO-as-code spec persists, but like the llms.txt exemplar it is a proposal-level fact captured here with no mechanism or adoption detail.

actionability.rationale: Two sentences of what-it-is with no schema fragment, tooling, or adoption guidance leave a reader nothing to build or decide with.

atomicity.rationale: It carries exactly one idea — declaratively define SLOs in YAML — statable in a single sentence.
